Hi Alex —

Great session earlier today — thanks for walking us through PulseForge's ingestion patterns and the latency targets you shared. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can lock a short orientation/demo (30 minutes) and surface the technical owners: 

What I heard (top-level):
- Need near-real-time vector updates for user events (sub-500ms tokenization + async embedding ingestion)
- Multi-tenant data isolation (per-namespace encryption and auditability)
- P99 generation latency target ~300ms for short prompts; ability to route to cheaper variants for backfill

Proposed next step: 30-minute intro/demo to show Redwood's serving flow, routing/fallback, and a live latency/cost demo for a sample workload. Please confirm which of the following windows works best for your team (PDT):

Option A: Tue Aug 10 — 09:00–09:30 PDT
Option B: Wed Aug 11 — 11:00–11:30 PDT
Option C: Thu Aug 12 — 14:00–14:30 PDT

Please also confirm who from PulseForge should join (technical lead / security / procurement). From our side: Priyom (solutions engineer) and Laura (CS lead) will join; I will run the product orientation.

Attachments: product-onepager.pdf (one-sheet) and RWD-MAP-v1.pdf (mutual action plan stub) — I'll drop a calendar invite once we have a slot.

Goals for the 30-min session:
- Validate fit for near-real-time embedding flow
- Walk the routing + isolation controls relevant to compliance
- Agree next technical deep-dive owners and success criteria for a pilot

If none of those slots fit, send 2–3 alternatives and we'll re-match calendars.

Thanks,
